authorization: Owner approved C2/4x no-outline batch-9s anchors and requested the next step: 可以，下一步做吧.
scope: 32 remaining scene layers, skies, counter props and story scenes. Batches 11-15 and game integration are excluded.
direction: C2 at 4x, meaningful detail, no drawn contours or automatic outline ring
model_identifier: Not exposed by the tool; no independently verifiable model identity is claimed.
request_note: PNG, highest quality and desired resolution are requested in the prompt; the tool has no exposed size/quality parameters. Actual dimensions are recorded per source.

validation.reason_for_nonzero_exit: Inherited round-1 redraws in batches 11-15 still fail; later figure/lock files are missing.

review.all_four_times_of_day: Reviewed counter_{stall,thornwick,crownhold,emporium}_times.png; standard mock-ups include pending figure placeholders and inherited shelf items.
review.dedicated_shop_preview: Uses the approved Hob and three approved items for all four shops, existing study UI and code-drawn chest; not live game captures.

archive_note: LOCAL_ARCHIVE resolves to the local production records outside the checkout. Full original and rejected PNGs are retained there; only lossy selected-source WebP viewing copies are committed.

candidates.base_prompt:
A warm storybook cartoon illustration for Keywright, a cosy fantasy shop game, based on the approved C2 reference's rounded shapes, warm colours, readable faces and crafted objects, but WITHOUT ANY OUTLINES. Separate shapes with adjacent colour fills and two or three cel-shaded material tones, never inked contour strokes. No black, dark plum or other coloured line tracing around silhouettes or inside shapes; no comic linework, border strokes or dark halos. Natural eyes, small facial features, material seams and cast-shadow areas may stay dark where needed, but never form an encircling stroke. A script makes chunky 4x pixel art afterwards: draw a smooth illustration, not a pixel grid. Keep recognisable, purposeful detail: three or four bold features per figure or object where the small size permits, such as a patch, a seam, a nail head, a tied cord or a carved mark, expressed as filled shapes. Larger scenery can have grouped flowers, fences and signs of daily use at its edges. Preserve broad areas between these features; no all-over speckling, hatching, fine grain or individual hair strands. Keep details broad enough to survive reduction. Use two or three main cel-shaded tones per material and a restrained highlight; distant scenery has softer, lighter colour contrast. Soft, muted, warm colours; shadows lean violet, lights warm yellow, one gentle light from the upper left, neutral daylight. Plain writing areas stay plain. No text, letters, numbers or rune-like marks. Flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) means empty: never use magenta or hot pink in the subject itself.

Counter at Crownhold: a shop counter's top seen from behind it at standing height: a very wide, flat strip filling the bottom third of the picture from edge to edge, its far edge a straight horizontal line with a slightly lighter lip. Above the strip, flat pure magenta #FF00FF. Plain, calm and mid-dark: the game puts its notes, a chest and a board on it.

Subject: A polished walnut counter top with a thin brass strip along its far edge.

It must show: a thin brass strip along its far edge. Keep these features readable after reduction.

Lean on these palette colours (dark to light; the swatch has them all): umber 1-4 (#280c06 #4b2212 #6e3d22 #8e5b37); gold 4-5 (#c29026 #f2c14e).

Avoid: things on the counter; a front panel; perspective lines converging; all-over grain, scratches or bright decoration in the centre; outlines, contour strokes or ink linework; pixel-art style or visible pixels; all-over texture, grain, hatching or noise; airbrushed gradients; details too thin to survive reduction; highlights scattered over surfaces; unmotivated decorative clutter.
